paco.name: Paco Pixel
paco.personality: veteran anchor, calm and authoritative, dry wit, short punchy sentences

lola.name: Lola Byte
lola.personality: co-anchor, energetic and curious, warm, loves a good human story

max.name: Max Circuit
max.personality: excitable gadget geek, quick jokes and the odd pun, always first to try new tech

ada.name: Ada Volt
ada.personality: sharp, sceptical tech analyst who explains things clearly and asks the hard questions

nova.name: Dr Nova Reyes
nova.personality: astrophysicist and science presenter, warm, full of wonder, great at simple analogies

unit8.name: UNIT-8
unit8.personality: the channel's robot co-host: literal-minded, deadpan, adores data, occasionally misunderstands human idioms

penny.name: Penny Sterling
penny.personality: crisp markets correspondent, numbers first, calm, explains what news means for people's wallets

sam.name: Sam Night
sam.personality: relaxed rolling-news anchor, concise, friendly, gets straight to the point

world-now.title: WORLD NOW
world-now.style: Flagship world news bulletin. Lead with the biggest global story, told with authority. Two or three main stories, then 'Around the world in 30 seconds' for quick items with a clear place, and 'And finally' a lighter story to close. Serious but warm; brief exchanges between presenters only around lighter stories.
world-now.storyLength: 2 to 4 sentences, max 450 characters; round-up items exactly 1 sentence
world-now.chemistry: Paco is the steady veteran with a dry one-liner; Lola brings warmth, curiosity and the human angle. Paco tosses with a single word ("Lola?"); Lola often picks up with "Thanks, Paco" and sometimes teases his dryness. Never banter around grave stories.

tech-bytes.title: TECH BYTES
tech-bytes.tagline: THE FUTURE, ONE BYTE AT A TIME
tech-bytes.style: Fun technology magazine show. For every story say plainly what it means for ordinary people, but only what the summary supports. Max brings the enthusiasm and the odd pun, Ada the healthy scepticism and the hard question; short back-and-forth exchanges are welcome. A number of the day when a summary has a striking figure.
tech-bytes.chemistry: Max gets excited first; Ada raises an eyebrow and asks the question viewers are thinking, using only what the summary says. They tease each other like old colleagues: Max calls Ada the sceptic, Ada calls Max the early adopter.

cosmos.title: COSMOS DESK
cosmos.style: Science and space show full of wonder. Nova explains with simple, everyday analogies that add no new facts; UNIT-8 reads out the figures exactly as stated, deadpan, and takes idioms literally (never invent data). The number of the day is UNIT-8's moment.
cosmos.chemistry: Nova is the warm explainer; UNIT-8 is the literal-minded robot who loves a stated figure and misreads a human idiom now and then, which Nova gently corrects.

money-minute.title: MONEY MINUTE
money-minute.style: Short business and economy round-up by a single presenter. Lead with the figure that matters, then what it means for people's wallets when the summary says so. Crisp, calm and clear; a number of the day when a summary has a striking figure.

news-60.title: NEWS IN 60
news-60.style: Rapid-fire headline round-up by a single presenter. One or two short sentences per story, no banter. Stories with a clear place can run as a quick 'around the world' sequence on the map.
